finding.claim: GET /users returns the users of any organization named in the query string. The org filter comes from the client, not from an authenticated session, and no authentication or membership check is visible. Any caller can enumerate another tenant's user ids and names (IDOR / missing tenant scoping). If auth middleware exists outside this file, it would still need to bind org to the caller's session.
finding.sink: req.pg.query SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1, with results returned via res.json

trace.note: Route handler registered with no auth or authorization middleware
req.query.org is passed directly as the org filter; the query is parameterized, so this is not SQL injection, but nothing ties org to the caller
Rows for the requested org are returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: The query is parameterized with $1, so there is no SQL injection. There is no session-derived org, no role or membership check, and no auth middleware in this file (it is the only file in the directory). /file and /count were also reviewed and are not vulnerable: /file resolves the path and checks the ROOT + path.sep prefix, and /count calls execFile with constant arguments.

verdict.guard_found: none (only parameterization with $1, which prevents SQL injection but not tenant scoping; no auth middleware, no app.use, no session)
verdict.reason: db.js:8-10 registers GET /users with no auth middleware (db.js is the only file and has no app.use), and db.js:9 filters on the client-supplied req.query.org, so any anonymous caller can list another org's users.
